title: Learning about informativeness
abstract: arXiv:2406.05299v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study whether individuals can learn the informativeness of their information technology through social learning. As in the classic sequential social learning model, rational agents arrive in order and make decisions based on the past actions of others and their private signals. There is uncertainty regarding the informativeness of the common signal-generating process. We show that in this setting asymptotic learning about informativeness is not guaranteed and depends crucially on the relative tail distributions of private beliefs induced by uninformative and informative signals. We identify the phenomenon of perpetual disagreement as the cause of learning and characterize learning in the canonical Gaussian environment.

translated_abstract: 我们研究个体能否通过社会学习来了解其信息技术的信息量。与经典的序贯社会学习模型一样，理性个体按顺序到达，并根据他人过去的行为和自己的私人信号做出决策。但对于共同的信号生成过程的信息量存在不确定性。我们证明，在这种设定下，关于信息量的渐近学习并不能得到保证，并且关键取决于由无信息信号和有信息信号所引致的私人信念的相对尾部分布。我们识别出永久分歧现象是学习成败的原因，并在标准的高斯环境中刻画了学习的特征。
tldr: 该论文研究个体能否通过社会学习了解其信息技术的信息量，发现渐近学习并不必然发生，而是取决于无信息信号与有信息信号所引致的私人信念的相对尾部分布，并识别出永久分歧现象是学习能否发生的关键原因。
